subject: host-effect-authorization.v12
protocol: Independent review under D-000; refute not confirm; did not author v1-v12; successor to v11 (Codex REJECT at HAE11-CX-01, frozen 4ec4c693...)
reviewerDisclosure: Three of v12's four claimed repairs answer findings I raised against v10 (IR-HEA10-B1, and by way of Codex HAE10-CX-01 the substance of my IR-HEA10-B2 and IR-HEA10-S1, plus IR-HEA10-S2). v12 also takes the specific remedy I named in my own v10 B1 note - re-scoping FC-CARRIER-SHAPE to the authorizationRecord side. That is a standing risk of confirmation bias in this review and I treated it as a reason for more scrutiny of those regions, not less. I re-derived each repair from v12's bytes rather than checking it against my own prior text, and the blocker below is inside the region I previously asked to have changed.
summary: The hygiene layer is clean and better than v10's: all seven prompt pins reproduce, all 37 measurable recordedInputs digests reproduce, and the six fail-closed and preview-denial regions are byte-identical to v11 (zero delta across failClosed, coveredActs, slice1EgressExecutionSide, joinBlockerDisposition, outcomeVocabulary and effectCommit). Every recited count is exact (19/19 closed members, 19/19 mapping destinations, 15/15 scope members). My IR-HEA10-S2 is properly repaired: the three deleted remasurement sentences are restored, wholeFileSha256Standing HISTORICAL-AT-D-032-RECORDING and liveWholeFileSha256 are added, environmentStanding's COORD entry becomes a historical/live object, and sectionExtractionRule now asserts the section still hashes 00085513... at the live COORD - which I verified independently at lines 1621-1654. My IR-HEA10-S1 is repaired (whenPresent is a closed source-identity object, not boolean true) and the substance of IR-HEA10-B2 is repaired (appliesTo now names both nullWhen and requiredWhen, each member carries an explicit domain, and a new unmatchedCarrier totality clause matches unmatchedSerializedClass). The repair of IR-HEA10-B1 does not hold. v12 retargets consentCarrierPredicateDomain.appliesTo[0] from the scope member to 'authorizationRecord.closedMembers[policyProvenance] nullWhen/requiredWhen' and declares the AR the authoritative discriminator layer - but it never adds nullWhen or requiredWhen to the AR policyProvenance member. Those keys do not exist there. The AR member carries the carrier conditional only inside its free-text semantics string, while the serialized scope member - the layer the same rule declares non-authoritative for the discriminator - is the only one carrying the structured predicates. The prose-only carrier I found at v10 is not removed; it is relocated from the discriminator to the predicate, one layer up.

findings.title: appliesTo[0] names nullWhen/requiredWhen on the authorizationRecord policyProvenance member; neither key exists there, so the layer declared authoritative carries the carrier predicate only in prose
findings.whatTheArtifactClaims: consentCarrierPredicateDomain.domain = 'authorizationRecord.consentCarrier'. Its rule: 'The discriminator is authorizationRecord.consentCarrier, a closed AR member. It is NOT a consentRecords[].scope member and MUST NOT be read from residualLimitation.' Its appliesTo[0] = 'authorizationRecord.closedMembers[policyProvenance] nullWhen/requiredWhen'. authorityClaim and honestyRepairsFromV11[1] both present this as the repair of IR-HEA10-B1.
whatIMeasured: authorizationRecord.closedMembers[14] is policyProvenance. Its complete key set is: name, nullable, required, semantics, type, union, whenPresent. It has no nullWhen key and no requiredWhen key.

consentRecordsScopeShape.members[10] is policyProvenance. Its complete key set is: name, nullWhen, nullWhenDomain, nullable, requiredWhen, requiredWhenDomain, sourceJoin, stringRefused, type, union, whenPresent. It has both keys, each with an explicit consentCarrier domain annotation.
Across all 19 authorizationRecord closed members, the only member carrying a nullWhen or requiredWhen key is actionSubtype. policyProvenance is not among them.

The v11->v12 delta confirms the retarget was deliberate and the keys were not created alongside it. appliesTo[0] changed from 'consentRecordsScopeShape.members[policyProvenance].nullWhen' to 'authorizationRecord.closedMembers[policyProvenance] nullWhen/requiredWhen'. In the same edit closedMembers[14] gained only type, union and the whenPresent sub-object, and had its semantics string rewritten. No predicate key was added.

The AR member's carrier conditional therefore lives entirely inside its semantics string: 'For pre-existing-policy: a source-identity object {authority, artifactPath, selector, digest}. Null with reason for invocation-time-naming. A string value refuses.'
findings.whyItIsABlocker: The repair's whole move is to relocate the carrier predicate from a layer where the discriminator is unavailable to a layer where it is a closed member. That move is only real if the predicate is actually expressed at the destination layer. It is not. A checker following appliesTo[0] to the AR member finds no predicate to evaluate; a checker following appliesTo[1] to the scope member finds the predicate but is forbidden by the same rule from reading the discriminator there ('It is NOT a consentRecords[].scope member') and by FC-CARRIER-SHAPE from requiring it there ('A validator MUST NOT require consentCarrier on consentRecords[].scope'). The structure is inverted relative to the claim: the authoritative layer has the discriminator but not the predicate, and the non-authoritative layer has the predicate but not the discriminator. Neither layer, taken as structure, is self-sufficient. What closes the gap is the AR member's prose - the one carrier form this artifact rejects everywhere else, including in this very fixture: FC-CARRIER-SHAPE's own passProperty ends 'Prose-only residualLimitation disclosure is not a substitute (FC-OUTCOME)', and FC-OUTCOME states 'A prose-only encoding fails.'
findings.relationToMyV10Finding: IR-HEA10-B1 was that the carrier DISCRIMINATOR had no structured home. v12 fixes that: consentCarrier is a closed AR member with closed values, and the mapping destination now names it as 'the structured discriminator' rather than routing it to residualLimitation. That half is genuinely repaired and I credit it. The defect that survives is one layer up - the PREDICATE that consumes the discriminator is unstructured at the layer the artifact designates as authoritative. This is the same failure mode, not a new one, which is why I am not treating v12's adoption of my suggested remedy as evidence the remedy landed.
findings.smallestRepair: Add nullWhen 'invocation-time-naming', requiredWhen 'pre-existing-policy', nullWhenDomain and requiredWhenDomain 'authorizationRecord.consentCarrier' to authorizationRecord.closedMembers[policyProvenance], mirroring the keys the scope member already carries. That makes appliesTo[0] resolve to real structure and costs nothing elsewhere. I name it to show the finding is narrow and repairable, not to author the repair.
findings.notRepairableByPrompt: PASS-NO-SCOPE-EFFECT does not reach this. Nothing moved; this is internal to the subject's own bytes.

findings.title: None of whenPresent's five constraints is exercised by a refuse case under the only carrier where policyProvenance is present-and-required
whatIMeasured: whenPresent declares five substantive constraints beyond kind/type/nullable: closedMembers [authority, artifactPath, selector, digest], digestEncoding '64-hex-lowercase-sha256', stringsNonEmptyBounded true, maxStringBytes 512, extrasRejected true.
policyProvenance is present-and-required under exactly one carrier value: pre-existing-policy.

FC-CARRIER-SHAPE's five parentRecords under pre-existing-policy are: [1] a well-formed four-member object -> accept-shape; [2] the string 'not-an-object' -> refuse; [4] null -> refuse. There is no pre-existing-policy record carrying a malformed OBJECT.

The only malformed object in the fixture is [3], {authority: 'x'}, and it sits under invocation-time-naming, where policyProvenance must be null. That record must refuse on carrier grounds alone, so a validator can return the expected refusal without ever evaluating closedMembers, digestEncoding, string bounds or extras.

This is not a v12 regression. v11 had the same misplacement; v12 swapped the carriers on parentRecords[2] and [3] and changed [4] from a string to null, which improves the null/string split but leaves the malformed-object case under the wrong carrier.
findings.whyItMatters: whenPresent is the substance of the HAE10-CX-01 and HAE11-CX-01 repairs - it is what replaced the unenumerable 'closedValuesWhenPresent: true' I raised at IR-HEA10-S1 and what makes strings refuse. The fixture that is cited as exercising it does not reach any of its five constraints in a refusing position. Missing members, a non-hex or uppercase digest, an empty or over-512-byte string, and an extra key are all currently untestable through FC-CARRIER-SHAPE. By the standard the artifact applies to itself elsewhere - FC-BOUND-SHAPE enumerates concrete parent records per variant precisely so each declared bound has a refusing case - this fixture is under-specified for the shape it was written to protect.
findings.suggestedDirection: Add at least one pre-existing-policy parentRecord with a malformed source-identity object (missing member, bad digest encoding, or extra key) resolving to refuse.

findings.title: v12 newly asserts a consentRecords[].scope.policyProvenance projection, and no fixture protects or tests it
whatIMeasured: doctorV4FieldMapping.destinations.policyProvenance changed in v12 from 'consentRecords[].scope.policyProvenance when carrier is pre-existing-policy' to 'authorizationRecord.policyProvenance object (and consentRecords[].scope.policyProvenance projection) when consentCarrier is pre-existing-policy; absent/null when invocation-time-naming. Never a bare string.' The word projection is new.

FC-ROUND-TRIP's passProperty enumerates what an attempted-act consent record may not drop or relabel: actor, actionSubtype, designContractRef digest, productAdmissionRefs digest/selector/standing, owners, auditIdentity, componentGenerationIdentity, admittedManifestDigest, authorized endpointSet. The substring policyProvenance does not occur in it. Neither does consentCarrier.
All five FC-CARRIER-SHAPE parentRecords carry layer 'authorizationRecord'. No parentRecord exercises the serialized scope, so the projection is asserted in the mapping and exercised nowhere.
authorizationRecord.notAGrant states the record 'does not survive the invocation', so the AR is not available to a later reader of the post-report.
findings.whyItMatters: policyProvenance is a member of the closed 15-member scope and therefore survives into the durable post-report, while the AR that governs it does not. v12 correctly forbids residualLimitation as the carrier, which means the carrier axis now has no durable structured representation at all. Combined with policyProvenance's absence from FC-ROUND-TRIP's protected enumeration, a consent record can drop or relabel scope.policyProvenance and no fixture class catches it - while the same fixture protects seven other scope members by name. The artifact newly claims a projection and supplies neither a fidelity test for it nor round-trip protection of it.
findings.whatIAmNotClaiming: I am not claiming the consent record must be self-validating on the carrier axis. D-032 makes doctor consent invocation-bound and not a grant, so consentCarrier not surviving may well be intended. The finding is narrower: a projection that v12 newly names should be enumerated in FC-ROUND-TRIP alongside the other projected members, or the projection language should be withdrawn.

predecessorFindingVerification.IR-HEA10-B1: PARTIALLY REPAIRED - discriminator half repaired, predicate half not. See IR-HEA12-B1. consentCarrier is now a closed AR member named as 'the structured discriminator', and destinations.consentCarrier no longer routes to residualLimitation ('residualLimitation may disclose the same value as prose but is not the carrier and is not a substitute'). consentCarrierPredicateDomain.domain moved from 'consentCarrier' to 'authorizationRecord.consentCarrier'. FC-CARRIER-SHAPE is re-scoped to the AR with an explicit 'A validator MUST NOT require consentCarrier on consentRecords[].scope'. What did not happen is the creation of the predicate keys at the AR that appliesTo[0] now names.
predecessorFindingVerification.IR-HEA10-B2: REPAIRED, credited in the artifact to Codex HAE10-CX-01. appliesTo now names both nullWhen and requiredWhen rather than nullWhen alone; the scope member carries both nullWhenDomain and requiredWhenDomain; and v12 adds unmatchedCarrier ('every legal consentCarrier value must select null policyProvenance or a well-formed source-identity object, never both, never neither, never a string'), which is the carrier-domain analogue of unmatchedSerializedClass whose absence I recorded at v10. The ungoverned-predicate hole is closed. The residual defect is that appliesTo's first target does not exist as structure, which is IR-HEA12-B1 rather than a survival of B2.
predecessorFindingVerification.IR-HEA10-S1: REPAIRED. closedValuesWhenPresent: true is gone from both layers. policyProvenance is now type object, union object-or-null, with a closed whenPresent source-identity shape at both the AR and the scope, plus stringRefused true on the scope member. The member's legal values are now enumerable, so doctorV4FieldMapping's totality rule can be discharged for it. The fixture does not exercise the new shape, which is IR-HEA12-S1.
predecessorFindingVerification.IR-HEA10-S2: REPAIRED, and more completely than I asked. All three sentences v10 had deleted are restored verbatim in remeasurementClause. The two-pin divergence I raised is now labelled at every site where it appears.
predecessorFindingVerification.CLAUDE-HEA9-S1 (not mine; recorded at ho: Verified as present and sound, since it touches the predicate-domain axis I am reviewing. authorizationRecord.actionSubtype now keys on the record's own literals (closedValuesWhenCA-1-HOST-HEAD, closedValuesWhenCA-4-HOST) with a perClassMap binding all four AR actionClass literals to their key; the serialized member gains per-class lists over CA-1..CA-4 with a perClassBinding; unmatchedSerializedClass now also requires the matching actionSubtype domain; and FC-SUBTYPE-CLASS supplies six parentRecords including cross-class refusals in both vocabularies (CA-1+KEYCHAIN and CA-1-HOST-HEAD+KEYCHAIN, CA-4+SPAWN and CA-4-HOST+SPAWN). predecessorFindingVerification.HAE11-CX-01: REPAIRED. policyProvenance's outer type is object at both layers with union object-or-null, matching whenPresent, and stringRefused true on the scope member. FC-CARRIER-SHAPE parentRecords[2] carries the string 'not-an-object' under pre-existing-policy resolving to refuse. I did not read the Codex v11 verdict text; I hashed it to verify the pin and derived the v11 defect from v11's own bytes, where members[10].type was 'string' while whenPresent already described an object.

verdictNote: REJECT at 1 blocker and 2 should-fix. v12 is a real generation of work and most of it holds: the remasurement scoping is restored and extended past what I asked for, the two-pin COORD divergence is now labelled everywhere it appears and I verified the live-COORD section claim rather than accepting it, the unenumerable closed-value assertion is replaced by a genuine closed source-identity shape, the carrier domain gains the totality clause it lacked, and the six fail-closed regions are byte-identical to v11. The blocker is narrow and mechanical. v12 retargeted consentCarrierPredicateDomain.appliesTo[0] onto the authorizationRecord's policyProvenance member and declared that layer authoritative, but never gave that member the nullWhen and requiredWhen keys the pointer names - its full key set is name, nullable, required, semantics, type, union, whenPresent. So the authoritative layer holds the discriminator and states the conditional only in prose, while the layer the same rule declares non-authoritative is the only one holding the conditional as structure. That is my v10 finding moved up one level rather than closed, and I hold it despite v12 having adopted the exact remedy I proposed, because the remedy was adopted in name at the pointer and not in the bytes it points at. The artifact already demonstrates the correct pattern one member away: actionSubtype carries per-class structured bindings on both the record side and the serialized side, with a perClassMap and a fixture that refuses cross-class values in both vocabularies. Applying that same symmetry to policyProvenance is, as far as I can measure, the whole of the blocker.
